before.exam_tip_html: Never answer a texture question with a single label on its own — examiners reward description that proves you actually heard the passage. A strong worked answer looks like this: "The cello introduces a scalic melody in its upper register while the viola and second violin provide a steady chordal accompaniment beneath, creating melody-dominated homophony" rather than just "it is homophonic". A very common mistake is confusing monophonic with homophonic: if you can hear more than one independent rhythm or more than one chord happening, it is no longer monophonic, even if the instruments sound closely blended — monophonic means genuinely one line (or that line doubled), nothing more.

When a question asks you to describe fusion in an extract, do not just list separate features ("there is a dhol and there is a synthesiser") — instead, phrase your answer to show how the elements interact, for example: "a sampled tumbi riff is looped over a programmed drum-machine beat, combining a traditional melodic timbre with a modern rhythmic texture"; examiners reward answers that explain the relationship between traditional and produced elements, not just their presence.

Do not simply describe the instruments you hear and stop there — examiners reward answers that link sonority to effect in a single connected sentence, for example: ‘the horn sustains a low harmony note while the flute and oboe alternate the melody in imitation, which fills the middle and top of the texture so the wind quintet sounds fuller than five solo lines’. A common mistake is naming instruments correctly but never saying what their combination achieves, which caps marks even when the identification is accurate.
